title: Geometric-stalk test and inverse-image stability of Tor intervals
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $T$ a scheme, $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and $a\le b$ integers. Geometric stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Then $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if for every geometric point $\bar t$ and every $A$-module $M$ the complex $K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. Consequently for every scheme morphism $u:U\to T$, the exact constant-coefficient inverse image $u^*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves each Tor interval.

proof.text: Assume $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. For a geometric point $\bar t$ and an arbitrary $A$-module $M$, apply the definition to the degree-zero constant module sheaf $\underline M[0]$. Its derived tensor with $K$ has zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$. The module-stalk cohomology comparison transfers this vanishing to its stalk at $\bar t$, and the constant-module tensor/stalk isomorphism identifies that stalk with $K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0]$. This proves the required stalk condition.

source.place: Tag 0DJJ (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), forward implication specialized to constant coefficients; tensor comparison from Tag 0DEN (lemma-check-K-flat-stalks)

proof.text: Conversely, let $\mathcal F$ be any $A_T$-module sheaf and $i\notin[a,b]$. The unbounded tensor/stalk comparison identifies $(K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal F[0])_{\bar t}$ with $K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\mathcal F_{\bar t}[0]$. The hypothesis, tested on the ordinary module $M=\mathcal F_{\bar t}$, makes its $i$-th cohomology zero at every $\bar t$. The module-stalk zero-detection criterion therefore gives $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal F[0])=0$. Quantifying over $\mathcal F$ and $i$ is exactly the definition of Tor amplitude.

For $u:U\to T$ and $K$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, the derived module pullback/stalk isomorphism gives $(u^*K)_{\bar v}\cong K_{u\circ\bar v}$ for every geometric point $\bar v$ of $U$. By the forward implication, tensoring the right-hand side with any ordinary $A$-module has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. The converse implication, now on $U$, gives the same Tor interval for $u^*K$.

lean.statement: theorem geometricStalk_torAmplitude_test (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (T : Scheme.{u}) (K : DerivedCategoryModule A T) (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b) : (DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A T a b K ↔ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T) (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (i : ℤ), i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).obj (((pointSmallEtale t).sheafFiber (A := ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ⊗ (_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) 0).obj M))) ∧ (∀ (U : Scheme.{u}) (f : U ⟶ T), DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A T a b K → DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A U a b ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))

reviewed_lean.note: lem-sf-etale-stalk-tor-test at 79f0a644: every clause matches the node. Ring any commutative A (Type u+1), no extra hypotheses; K an unbounded DerivedCategoryModule; a ≤ b kept; the iff ranges over all geometric points (Ω : Type u, algebraically closed) and all modules (ModuleCat.{u+1} A); i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero(H^i(stalk K ⊗ M[0])), where ⊗ is the derived monoidal structure on D(ModuleCat A) (checked by #synth); the pullback conjunct holds for arbitrary f with the same interval, via upperStar.mapDerivedCategory, which is the framework's own D((f)^*[A]).
